style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression, long-lens view of industrial infrastructure. An unbranded, heavy electric semi-truck connected to a massive illuminated charging umbilical in a sprawling freight yard at dusk. Extreme asymmetry, low-angle with scale contrast, positioning the truck off-center against towering distribution center walls. Stacked overlapping layers of structure with crystal-clear telephoto distance clarity, flat compressed perspective. Deep industrial contrast, sharp directional amber yard lighting slicing through deep blue ambient twilight, highlighting the brushed metal and matte polymer textures of the vehicle. No people, no haze, no text.
negative_prompt: text, words, letters, numbers, watermark, signature, logo, typography, branding, UI, people
rationale: The story centers on heavy industrial freight and the physical infrastructure required to move it. A compressed telephoto shot grounds the abstract financial mechanics of certificates in the stark, massive reality of electric logistics.
cue: moves the cost of the last mile
subject: unbranded heavy electric semi-truck at a charging depot
core_thesis: Shippers are relying on environmental certificates rather than fuel savings to cover the persistent cost gap of operating heavy electric trucks.
core_conflict: High diesel prices vs. the even higher total operating costs of electric heavy freight.
composition: extreme asymmetry, low-angle with scale contrast
